nameStory: The Banded Pennant gets its name from the striking black bands that stretch across its wings like bold stripes on a flag or pennant. These dark markings are so distinctive and sharply defined that they make this dragonfly look like it's flying around with tiny banners attached to its body.
description: The Banded Pennant is a medium-sized dragonfly that belongs to the skimmer family, known for their habit of perching on vegetation near water. At about 1.3 inches long, it's easily recognized by the dramatic black bands and markings that decorate its clear wings. These striking wing patterns make it one of the more distinctive dragonflies you'll encounter around ponds and lakes. Like all dragonflies, it's a skilled aerial hunter that catches mosquitoes and other small flying insects on the wing.

idTips.label: Wing markings
idTips.description: Look for extensive, sharply defined black bands and patches across the wings - these dark markings are crisp and bold, not fuzzy or faded, creating a striking contrast against the clear wing membrane

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: About 1.3 inches long with a relatively compact body compared to larger dragonflies - roughly the length of a large paperclip

idTips.label: Wing pattern variation
idTips.description: The amount of black on the wings varies considerably - some individuals have very bold, extensive markings while others (especially in northern areas) show more modest dark patches

idTips.label: Perching behavior
idTips.description: Often seen perched on vegetation near water with wings held horizontally - when at rest, those distinctive wing bands are clearly visible and make identification easy

idTips.label: Flight pattern
idTips.description: Flies with the typical skimmer style of short bursts from perch to perch, rather than continuous patrolling - watch for quick darts out to catch prey before returning to the same or nearby perch

habitat: Look for Banded Pennants around still or slow-moving freshwater habitats including ponds, lakes, marshes, and roadside ditches. They prefer areas with plenty of emergent vegetation like cattails and sedges where they can perch while hunting. You'll often spot them in sunny, open areas around water rather than shaded woodland ponds.

seasonality.spring: Adults begin emerging in late spring and early summer. Look for fresh individuals with pristine wing markings near breeding waters.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity period when adults are most abundant and easily observed. This is the best time to see their dramatic courtship flights and territorial behaviors around water.
seasonality.fall: Adults may persist into early fall in warmer areas, though they become less active as temperatures drop. Wing markings may appear slightly faded on older individuals.
seasonality.winter: Not active - adults die off with the first hard frosts, while eggs and larvae overwinter underwater in ponds and lakes.

funFact: Despite their bold wing markings making them seem easy targets for predators, Banded Pennants are actually masters of deception - those striking black bands can create optical illusions during flight that make it harder for birds to track their exact position and speed!
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with other pennant dragonflies, especially the Halloween Pennant which also has dark wing markings. The key difference is that Halloween Pennants have amber or yellow patches mixed with their dark markings, while Banded Pennants have primarily black markings on clear wings. Think 'pure bands' for Banded Pennants versus 'Halloween colors' for Halloween Pennants.
contextualKnowledge: The term 'pennant' in dragonfly names refers to the wing markings that resemble flags or banners, not the triangular sports pennants you might think of. All members of the Celithemis genus are called pennants because of their distinctively patterned wings that look like tiny decorative flags.
compareHints: Among the pennant dragonflies, the Banded Pennant stands out for having the most sharply contrasted black and clear wing pattern. Halloween Pennants mix orange and black like their namesake holiday, while Calico Pennants have a more mottled, patchwork appearance. The Banded Pennant's markings are the most 'graphic' - think bold black stripes rather than mixed colors or subtle patches.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Among the pennant dragonflies, the calico has the most irregular, patchy wing pattern compared to its relatives.

Among its pennant relatives in New England, the Halloween Pennant is the only one with bright orange wings - the Calico Pennant has clear wings with dark markings, while the Banded Pennant has amber wings but lacks the extensive orange coloration.

Among the pennant species, Martha's Pennant has its own unique wing pattern that separates it from the Calico Pennant's spotted wings, the Halloween Pennant's orange and brown bands, and the Banded Pennant's distinct banding.
